To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the erythromycin resistance genes in C. reinhardi are nuclear and chloroplast, 2) erythromycin binding to chloroplast ribosomes is a useful tool for studying chloroplast ribosome structure and 3) there are interactions between genes that specify different ribosome components.
erythromycin resistance in C. reinhardi is a property of the chloroplast ribosomes and that the chloroplast ribosomal RNA and proteins are coded for in the chloroplast DNA.

the chloroplast ribosomes of Chlamy-domonas reinhardi have at least five different loci affecting ribosomal proteins, each locus is unlinked to the other loci, and the ribosomes have at least three sites of action for antibiotics affecting protein synthesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a genetic approach to the structure of the ribosome, and with the relationship between ribosome structure and the mechanism of action of antibiotics.--This research was supported by National Institutes of Health Grant GM 17409 and by the National Science Foundation.
the structure of the chloroplast ribosomes in Chlamy domonas reinhardi, and with the genetic control of this structure.
the structure and organization of chloroplast ribosomal RNA and protein.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the chloroplast ribosomal proteins in Chlamy-dononas reinhardi are encoded by a number of different loci, both nuclear and chloroplast, that are genetically linked and that the ribosomal proteins are not randomly distributed on the ribosomal subunits.
the ribosome contains at least 10 different components, each of which may be specified by a different locus.
the erythromycin resistance mutations in Chlamy-domonas are a series of genetic alterations of the chloroplast ribosomal proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the chloroplast ribosomes are complex, with many different components, some of which are encoded in the chloroplast genome and some in the nuclear genome.
the chloroplast ribosomes of Chlamy domonas reinhardi are composed of at least eight different components, each specified by a different gene.
the ribosome is a highly integrated structure.--A model is proposed for the structure of the chloroplast ribosomes in Chlamy-domonas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the chloroplast ribosomes of C. reinhardi are composed of a number of distinct polypeptides, and that the genes for at least some of these are not clustered in the chloroplast genome.

the erythromycin resistance mutations are affecting different parts of the chloroplast ribosomal protein, and the ribosomes are interacting with each other in a way that is affecting the binding of the erythromycins.
the chloroplast ribosomes of Chlamy-domonas are not homogeneous in composition, as had been assumed, but consist of a number of different species.
